item.title: VCF 9.1.1 - DTGW & VNA: the route controller within me - Part 2
item.description:
Introduction

Sometimes sequels are better than the first one – take Batman, for example. The Dark Knight was already a blast. Maybe this second article about the route controller will go just as well, and it might even be more popular with you guys than the first one. Anyway, my vacation is over, and now I finally have more time to take a closer look at VCF 9.1.1 – and wow, what can I say? I actually thought VCF 9.1.1 would just be a minor update, but there’s been a lot going on in VCF Networking in particular. And just like that, we’re back in the networking rabbit hole, and I’ve been tinkering with a test setup for several days now to properly demonstrate the new features of the Route Controller.

item.title: VCF 9.1 - DTGW & VNA: the route controller within me
item.description:
Introduction

Oh no, not another one of those blogs—don’t you ever get tired of VPCs? To be honest, no, because VCF 9.1 offers a ton of new possibilities in this area, and I’m sure we’re still a long way from discovering its full potential. This article will focus on how to apply the Distributed VXLAN Connectivity Model in practice and in the lab. I hope you’ve brought enough coffee, because I’m afraid this might turn into another long journey down the rabbit hole.
